items.title: Mattamy Homes pitches 141-unit development in Mississauga
items.summary: Mark 10 years since the band's final show with Gord Downie. … 18 stores are already open across the province according to … Three modular mid-rise buildings are proposed on Ninth Line; a public meeting is set for Sept. 21. Three six-storey apartment buildings with a total of 141 units are being proposed at 6344 Ninth Line in Mississauga. The City of Mississauga is reviewing a proposal for three modular six-storey apartment buildings with a total of 141 units at 6344 Ninth Line, south of Doug Leavens Boulevard. The application by Mattamy Homes seeks to change the zoning bylaw to permit the development. , said additional landscape and public realm enhancements are also proposed around the perimeter of the site.

items.title: Motorcyclist seriously injured in Hwy. 401 crash in Mississauga
items.summary: A motorcyclist has been rushed to hospital after a crash with a vehicle on Highway 401 in Mississauga. m. Monday. A 53-year-old man was taken to hospital with serious, life-threatening injuries. It’s unknown whether anyone else was injured in the crash. The eastbound express lanes were closed from Winston Churchill to Mavis Road for several hours and the investigation is still ongoing.

items.title: New bylaw better protects renters from unlawful renovictions in Mississauga
items.summary: New rules aimed at better protecting renters in Mississauga will be in place in two weeks. The City of Mississauga’s Rental Repairs and Renovations Licensing Bylaw, to take effect Sept. 1, will prevent tenants from being unjustly evicted by landlords who say they’re planning major repairs to the property — a practice known as renovictions. Adopted by city council in April, the new bylaw “increases protections for tenants who face eviction when their landlord requires them to move out for extensive renovations or repairs,” city officials said earlier. The city noted on Monday the bylaw, which works in tandem with the Ontario Residential Tenancies Act to better protect renters from unlawful renovictions, was developed with input from tenants, landlords and community groups across Mississauga. “These changes will help make the eviction process clearer and fairer, while reducing housing instability and helping protect the city’s supply of affordable rental housing,” officials said. Renovictions have become more common in recent years, prompting Mississauga municipal politicians to take action in defence of city renters.

items.title: Lanes closed for serious motorcycle crash on Highway 401 in Mississauga
items.summary: Lanes on Highway 401 in Mississauga were closed on Monday afternoon after a two-vehicle crash involving a motorcycle. m. A 53-year-old motorcycle rider was taken to hospital with serious injuries, police said. There was no further information on the rider or any other injuries in the crash. Police said the investigation was ongoing. The express lanes were closed from Winston Churchill Boulevard. There is no word on when the lanes will reopen. items.title: Armed robbery probe leads to Mississauga suspects; 2 Brampton teens charged earlier
items.summary: Three people from Mississauga have now been charged in connection with a police investigation into an armed robbery that took place more than a year ago in a small central Ontario community. Ontario Provincial Police said the charges are related to a May 7, 2025 robbery of a financial institution in Keene, just southeast of Peterborough. m. that day, three culprits carrying weapons entered the bank and fled a short time later with an undisclosed amount of cash, according to investigators. Peterborough County OPP said descriptions of suspects and a getaway vehicle, which were provided at the time to police, led to the arrest a short time later of two teens from Brampton, one aged 16 and the other 17. The three subsequent arrests were made last month after further investigation “uncovered information regarding the planning and execution of the robbery,” police said in a news release late last week. On July 9, OPP officers arrested a suspect, now aged 19, at a home in Mississauga. The person was charged with conspiracy to commit an indictable offence and subsequently appeared in Peterborough court, police said. On July 22, two additional suspects, who were already in custody on unrelated matters at the Central North Correctional Centre in Penetanguishene, were arrested and charged in relation to the May 2025 robbery, according to police. Those suspects, aged 19 and 20 and both of Mississauga, are also charged with conspiracy to commit an indictable offence. Both have subsequently appeared before a Justice of the Peace and were remanded in custody with future court dates set, police said.

items.title: Mississauga's Priciest Home Sales Last Month Still Closed Below Asking, Zoocasa Data Shows
items.summary: According to INsauga, citing data from real estate platform Zoocasa, the most expensive homes sold in Mississauga last month all went for more than $2 million, even as the broader market continues to favour buyers over sellers. INsauga reports that every one of the top sales closed below its original list price, a trend Zoocasa says reflects a market that remains sluggish for sellers despite continued demand for multi-million-dollar properties. The single highest sale, according to the report, was a five-bedroom, seven-bathroom home just south of Square One Shopping Centre with more than 8,000 square feet of finished living space, two gas fireplaces, a finished basement with a games area and wet bar, and an exercise area and playroom. That property sold for $2,150,000, below its $2,299,900 asking price. Zoocasa's list also included a four-bedroom, six-bathroom home on a wide, treed lot in Lakeview, close to Lakefront Promenade Park and Lake Ontario, with a bright family room and kitchen and no visible rear neighbours thanks to its deep lot. INsauga notes the figures come from Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data on July sales activity.

items.title: Police Still Searching for Family of Woman Who Died After Saturday Night Fall Into Lake Ontario
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel police still have not identified the woman who died after falling into Lake Ontario at Jack Darling Memorial Park over the weekend, as investigators work to locate and notify her next of kin. INsauga reports the woman was swept into the water Saturday night and rushed to hospital, where she was pronounced dead a short time later. Police said Monday morning that no further details, including her age, will be released until her family has been notified. Investigators have not said whether the woman was alone or with others before she ended up in the lake. INsauga notes Jack Darling Memorial Park covers more than 20 acres along the Lake Ontario shoreline a few kilometres west of Port Credit Harbour, near where the Credit River empties into the lake. The park is one of the city's largest and most popular waterfront green spaces, with picnic areas, tennis courts, a beach, a leash-free zone, a spray pad, two playgrounds and a stretch of the Waterfront Trail running through it.

items.title: After 20 Years in British Columbia, 5X Fest Brings Its Panjabi Arts Celebration to Mississauga
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, 5X Fest, described as Canada's leading Panjabi arts organization, is holding its first event outside British Columbia this month at the city's historic Small Arms Inspection Building. The two-day festival, running August 21 and 22 and powered by CBC, marks the first time in the event's 20-year history that it has come to Ontario. The city says the weekend includes the 5X Art Party x Inkquisitive and 5X Blockparty, bringing internationally recognized artists together with a new generation of South Asian creatives. The Art Party event doubles as the final stop on the 15-Year World Tour of Panjabi artist Amandeep Singh, known as Inkquisitive, who will host an artist's talk, display original artworks and run a live auction of previously unreleased pieces. According to the city, the festival is made possible through a partnership with Mississauga Film and Music and support from Visit Mississauga, and organizers say it adds a major Panjabi arts and music event to Mississauga's cultural calendar. Both events are rain or shine and located near multiple public transit options, the city notes.

items.title: 5 charged, including 2 youths, in fatal double shooting on Brampton school grounds
items.summary: A 21-year-old and two 17-year-olds from Brampton are facing two charges each of first-degree murder, after a shooting on school grounds in Brampton that took the lives of one man and one youth in April, Peel police say.

items.title: Mississauga to Require Landlords to Get a City Licence Before Ordering Renovation-Related Evictions
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a new bylaw taking effect September 1 will require landlords to apply for a city licence within seven days of issuing an N13 Notice, the legal step used when a tenant must vacate for major repairs or renovations. The city says the Rental Repairs and Renovations Licensing By-law was developed with input from tenants, landlords and community groups, and is meant to add oversight to a process that has sometimes been used to permanently push out tenants under the guise of renovations, a practice known as renovicting. City officials explain that under Ontario law, an N13 Notice only applies when the work is significant, requires a building permit and requires the unit to be vacated, and that the notice itself is not an eviction order, since only the Landlord and Tenant Board can actually order an eviction. According to the city, tenants do not have to move out immediately just because they've received an N13 Notice. The new licensing requirement is intended to make the eviction process clearer and fairer while reducing housing instability and protecting the city's supply of affordable rental housing, officials said. The bylaw takes effect Sept. 1, 2026.

items.title: Dixie Road Southbound Lanes Shut All Week for Peel Region Storm Sewer Work
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Region has closed all southbound lanes of Dixie Road in Mississauga's east end this week while crews replace a section of storm sewer between Blundell Road and Caterpillar Road. INsauga reports the closure runs south of Dundas Street East and north of The Queensway East, and is scheduled to last through Friday. Mississauga Ward 1 Coun. Stephen Dasko told residents in an online notice that the work is happening night and day, covering a stretch from 80 metres south of Blundell Road to 180 metres north of Caterpillar Road. INsauga notes the project is one of several similar infrastructure upgrades already underway or planned across the city as aging pipes and sewers get replaced. A short distance west, INsauga reports Peel Region crews are also preparing to rehabilitate the Lower Cooksville Trunk Sewer, a system Mississauga Ward 7 Coun. Dipika Damerla has described as critical infrastructure carrying wastewater from homes and businesses in the area to treatment facilities. That project is expected to bring partial park and trail closures along with construction noise and dust starting this summer.

The rescue happened in “challenging conditions” with high winds and waves measuring two to three metres, say police. Nine people were found “clinging” to a boat in Lake Ontario after Peel police say they responded to a distress call involving a capsized vessel near Mississauga on Saturday evening. m. on Aug. 15 after receiving reports about a flipped boat near Port Credit Harbour Marina. An overturned boat was located about 50 metres south of the Ridgetown breakwall and nine people were found “clinging to the vessel,” said police. The rescue happened in “challenging conditions” with high winds and waves measuring two to three metres, say police. All nine people were “safely rescued” and taken to a nearby marina, police say. Those rescued had minor cuts and no major injuries were reported, added the Peel force.
